piece.title: String Quartet No.12 in F major, Op.96 (“American”)
piece.why: The famous viola opening: the theme starts in the viola under violin tremolo, moves to Violin I, then trades between cello and Violin I and cascades up through all four parts.

plan.summary: The tune starts in the viola (bars 2–8) and moves up to Violin 1 from bar 9, and the cover follows it. Tenor sax plays the opening Violin 1 notes in bar 1 (the only line sounding there), then the whole viola line. Alto sax plays the broken-chord figure first, then takes the Violin 1 tune, switching octave at phrase points so it stays in range. Baritone sax holds the cello bass throughout and covers Violin 2's low repeated Ds in bar 18, where that line is the bass.

assignments.reason: Bar 1 is just Violin 1's F/A figure on its own. The tenor plays it two octaves down so the opening is heard and sits low, like a bass.
The whole viola line at written pitch: the opening tune, inner harmony in bars 9–16, then the answering phrases. It's one continuous part in the tenor's warm middle register.
Violin 2's broken F-major chord figure at written pitch. It sits just above the tenor's tune.
The tune moves up to Violin 1 here. Playing it an octave down puts the high C6/D6 notes in the alto's comfortable range.
From bar 16 the tune drops low (down to B-flat 3), so the alto plays it at written pitch.
The last bar climbs to A5, above the alto's top note, so this one bar goes down an octave and the alto still finishes the tune.
The cello bass line at written pitch, from the F pedal to the moving arpeggios. Only the low D2 in bar 9 goes up an octave.
The cello rests in bar 18, and Violin 2's repeated Ds are the lowest line there. The bari plays them an octave down to keep the bass going.
The bari goes back to the cello bass line for the last two bars.

dropped.reason: Violin 1 only plays a high F/A broken-chord figure here, the same F chord the alto plays from Violin 2, and some of it is above the alto's range.
No player is free once the alto takes the tune. In bars 13–16 this is a secondary counter-line, and the rest is harmony the tenor and bari already cover.
Harmony filler, already covered by the tenor and bari, and no player is free.
The viola hasn't really started yet. The tenor uses this bar for the Violin 1 opening figure.
The cello rests here. The bari plays Violin 2's low Ds, which are the bass line in this bar.
